title: slabless-scratch-recycler-and-kv-compactor-to-reduce-peak-workspace
author: Nikhil Rao
description: Motivation: reduce peak GPU workspace and fragmentation across long-running inference workloads by avoiding slab-only scratch allocation and compacting KV cache segments opportunistically. This PR introduces a slabless scratch recycler that reuses freed scratch ranges without forcing expensive slab promotion and a background KV compactor that coalesces small KV segments into larger contiguous windows to reduce overall workspace and page table churn. The design targets cases where long prefix sequences and variable batch shapes cause transient high-water marks in device memory. Implementation summary: 1) scratch recycler: replace the monolithic slab allocator with a hybrid fast-path where small transient allocations are served from recycled free ranges and larger allocations fall back to an arena; recycler keeps a size-classed free-list with LRU eviction to avoid unbounded fragmentation; includes safe concurrency via epoch-based reclamation to avoid stalls on inference threads. 2) KV compactor: background compaction worker that merges fragmented KV pages when safe (no active references) and uses a lightweight bloom fingerprint to skip already-coalesced regions; compaction is throttled by latency headroom and configured SLO budget. 3) Scheduler integration: continuous-batching scheduler now queries recycler headroom and KV compaction load before bumping max-concurrent-seqs; this reduces peak workspace under bursts. 4) Activation checkpointing tweak: opportunistic lightweight checkpoint compression for large linear layers by storing XOR-deltas for low entropy activations when compression improves memory by >8%. Benchmarks: internal suite on g4dn-type nodes shows median peak-device-memory reduction of 26% on a 7B LLM test harness (single-stream heavy prefix mix), tail (p99) reduction of 18% across mixed batch sizes, and cost-per-token improvement of 9% due to fewer OOM/eviction events; latency regression was <1.5% for median requests and within SLO for 99th percentile after adaptive throttling. Backwards compatibility: all runtime APIs unchanged; feature gated behind config: runtime.scratch_recycler.enabled and runtime.kv_compactor.enabled. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pools with canary_fraction=0.05, monitor workspace_high_water and eviction_rate; automatic rollback on sustained increase in latency or error rate. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for recycler freelist and epoch reclamation - [x] deterministic reproducible microbench harness for KV compaction - [x] integration tests for scheduler gating - [x] bench regressions and cost analysis documented - [x] docs and tuning notes added. Related tickets: ENG-4021 (memory-pressure investigation), ENG-4075 (kv-cache fragmentation). Risks and mitigations: compaction can increase device activity; so compaction uses conservative default thresholds and requires explicit enable for private deployments. Caution: some workloads with extremely high allocation churn may need tuned class thresholds; guidance added to docs. This description is a continuous single field with design, benchmarks, rollout plan and checklist.
commits: refactor(runtime): introduce slabless scratch recycler with size-class LRU free lists
perf(kv): add background kv compactor with bloom-indexed coalescer
chore(scheduler): consult memory headroom before increasing concurrent sequences
feat(checkpointing): opportunistic xor-delta activation checkpointing and compression heuristic
fix(allocator): race fix in epoch reclamation under heavy concurrent frees
docs: add tuning guide for scratch recycler and kv compactor
review_comments: Ava Thompson: Nice design, Nikhil. Two high-level concerns: (1) how do we ensure compaction doesn't thrash PCIe bandwidth during busy windows; (2) can we reliably get rid of slab promotion without regressing allocation latency? Please add microbench numbers for alloc/free latency.
Author (Nikhil Rao): Added alloc/free membench in the benchmark suite and throttling gate for compaction. Compaction bandwidth capped to 20% by default and adaptive to observed tail latency.
Marcus Li: The epoch reclamation change looks good but caught a subtle ABA possibility in the freelist. Please add the compare-exchange backoff change I suggested.
Author: Addressed with exponential backoff and additional CAS loop comments; added a deterministic test that previously hung.
Priya Nair: Can we expose a per-pool config for recycler thresholds? Some customers might want aggressive compaction.
Author: Added runtime.scratch_recycler.size_classes and .max_reuse_window in defaults and docs.
Diego Morales (approval): Benchmarks acceptable, +1 for staged canary plan.
ci_checks: unit: pass (all allocator and kv unit tests)
perf-bench: pass (median memory reduction 26%, p99 within SLO)
release_notes: Introduce a slabless scratch recycler and background KV compactor to reduce peak GPU workspace and fragmentation. Default disabled for private installs; enabled for hosted gradually. Expected memory reductions up to ~30% in heavy-prefix workloads and lower cost-per-token for many inference patterns. See docs/runtime/memory_tuning.md for tuning.
